metric_rationale: This metric calculates the proportion of trials where the subject's choice matches the prediction of the Take The Best (TTB) heuristic. By design, TTB and Tallying make diametrically opposed predictions on most trials (and Tallying predicts a tie on the rest). Therefore, data simulated under TTB will yield a metric value close to 1 (subject to noise), while data simulated under Tallying will yield a metric value close to 0 (since it consistently picks the opposite option or guesses). This large mean difference, combined with low per-subject variance due to the consistent trial structure, ensures high discriminability.

This metric isolates 'conflict trials' where Tallying and Take The Best make strictly opposite predictions. By computing the proportion of times the subject's choice aligns with the Take The Best prediction on these trials, we generate a stark contrast between the two models. Data generated by TTB will yield scores near 1 (minus noise), while data generated by Tallying will yield scores near 0 (plus noise). The high number of conflict trials in the design ensures low within-subject variance, making it highly discriminative at the subject level.
